answer: Time-locked collateral bonding counters Sybil attacks by requiring participants to commit funds across a validation terrace before issuing actions. Rather than spawning a dense nebula of ephemeral clones, an adversary must incur the verifiable opportunity cost of locked capital for each registered vertex. This economic friction binds identity creation directly to liquidity. A critical limitation is that capital requirements create a plutocratic bias, heavily penalizing resource-poor agents.
